correctness.rationale: Taking the trace of a power of the rank-one product gives the off-diagonal block A=B^{circ r}; the SVD gives the full spectrum 1±s_j(A). For r<1 the constant-vector test is strict unless B is a permutation. For r>1 each nonsingleton component has all row and column sums of A strictly below one (an entry 1 would isolate a row-column pair), giving the common-ray criterion. Jensen gives the global fractional edge bound; equality in the nonnegative symmetric dilation forces degree saturation on a Perron support component, hence full uniform overlap by strict row/column Jensen. Each B_j B_j^T is irreducible, positive semidefinite and stochastic; its simple top eigenvalue gives exactly one critical branch. Differentiation with left and right constant unit vectors gives -h_j for the leading singular value. Taking the maximum over finitely many branches gives the opposite max/min entropy selections and the strict spectral gap to all nonleading branches gives the asserted local inertia.
residual_risks: The replay is finite numerical corroboration; the proof establishes the exact claims. The near-critical neighborhood and remainder are basis-dependent. No Lean verification or expert attestation was performed.

evidence: The necessary universal fidelity-power bound does not decide positivity for an individual pair; positivity at r=1 for pure ensembles is prior. Vuong–Osaka cover triples of positive operators for 1/2≤r≤1, and their four-point remark supplies a dimension-two MUB witness. For the bistochastic bipartite dilation H_j, rho(H_j^{circ r})=||B_j^{circ r}||_2, and the classical pressure derivative at one is -h_j.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves when a widely used fidelity-derived Gram matrix loses positivity on two complete bases, addressing more than a bad example. The support components identify which modes lose positivity and predict the two sides of the edge from different measurable entropies; with unequal component entropies or a shared ray the asymmetry is concrete. The sharp MUB uniqueness and the arbitrary-support classification make the answer useful despite elementary tools.
residual_risks: No extension to general ensembles, many unrelated bases, or uniform near-critical scale is established.
